metadata.name: [GCP GKE OTel] Node ephemeral storage nearly full
metadata.description: Fires for each GKE node whose ephemeral storage (boot disk) used over total is at least 85% now and in every reported minute of the cluster's last 15 minutes of data, with at least 12 of those minutes reported, so a new node or sparse data can't fire on a few samples. The 15 minutes are counted back from the cluster's newest sample, because GKE metrics reach Elasticsearch several minutes late; the 30-minute rule window leaves room for that delay. The kubelet starts garbage-collecting images at 85%, and on GKE it sets DiskPressure and evicts pods when less than 10% of total is free, so this is the warning before evictions. Total is the denominator because used over allocatable regularly exceeds 100%. Uses GKE system metrics, so it covers every cluster. Inode exhaustion also causes DiskPressure and is caught by the node condition rule. Nodes that stopped reporting more than 5 minutes before their cluster's newest sample are ignored.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.gke.otel-*
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "k8s_node"
    AND (`metrics.kubernetes.io/node/ephemeral_storage/used_bytes` IS NOT NULL
      OR `metrics.kubernetes.io/node/ephemeral_storage/total_bytes` IS NOT NULL)
// Latest used and total boot-disk bytes per node and minute. They can arrive in separate documents.
| STATS used_bytes = MAX(LAST_OVER_TIME(`metrics.kubernetes.io/node/ephemeral_storage/used_bytes`)),
        total_bytes = MAX(LAST_OVER_TIME(`metrics.kubernetes.io/node/ephemeral_storage/total_bytes`))
    BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location, resource.attributes.cluster_name,
       resource.attributes.node_name, bucket = TBUCKET(1 minute)
// Newest sample of each cluster, for the per-cluster freshness rule
| INLINE STATS cluster_newest = MAX(bucket)
    BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location, resource.attributes.cluster_name
// Judge the cluster's last 15 minutes of data rather than the last 15 minutes of clock time: metrics reach
// Elasticsearch several minutes late (Cloud Monitoring delay plus the receiver's polling interval).
| WHERE bucket >= cluster_newest - 15 minutes
// Used over total, not allocatable: GKE sets DiskPressure and evicts pods when free space drops below 10% of total
| EVAL minute_utilization = CASE(total_bytes > 0, TO_DOUBLE(used_bytes) / total_bytes, NULL)
| STATS used_bytes = LAST(used_bytes, bucket) WHERE used_bytes IS NOT NULL,
        total_bytes = LAST(total_bytes, bucket) WHERE total_bytes IS NOT NULL,
        min_utilization = MIN(minute_utilization),
        reported_minutes = COUNT(minute_utilization),
        last_seen = MAX(bucket),
        cluster_newest = MAX(cluster_newest)
    BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location, resource.attributes.cluster_name,
       resource.attributes.node_name
| EVAL latest_utilization = CASE(total_bytes > 0, TO_DOUBLE(used_bytes) / total_bytes, NULL),
       used_gib = used_bytes / 1073741824.0,
       total_gib = total_bytes / 1073741824.0

data.content:
## Node ephemeral storage nearly full

The node's boot disk has stayed at or above 85% used (`latest_utilization`, `min_utilization`) in every reported minute of the cluster's last 15 minutes of data (`reported_minutes`). GKE evicts pods with `DiskPressure` at 90%.

### Triage
1. Open **[GCP OTel] GKE Node Detail** for the node. **Ephemeral storage used vs allocatable vs total** shows how fast it fills; **Log volume by type** shows whether system or workload logging drives it; **Inodes free vs total** shows inode use.
2. Image garbage collection runs from 85%. If usage doesn't drop, the space is held by container writable layers, `emptyDir` volumes or logs rather than unused images.
3. Pod series carry no node label. Use **[GCP OTel] GKE Cluster Detail** and the Pods dashboard's ephemeral storage column to find pods with large ephemeral storage use in the cluster.

### Remediation
- Set ephemeral storage requests and limits on workloads that write locally, and move large scratch data to persistent volumes.
- Reduce log verbosity of noisy workloads.
- Enlarge the node pool's boot disk, or use a machine type with local SSDs for ephemeral storage.

### Notes
- Raise or lower the 0.85 threshold in both utilization conditions of the last `WHERE`; keep it below 0.9 to warn before evictions.
- The 15 minutes are counted back from the cluster's newest sample, not from the clock, because data arrives several minutes late. A new node needs at least 12 reported minutes.
